WITH busy AS (
                     SELECT repo_id, count(*) AS n FROM jobs WHERE status = 'running'
                     GROUP BY repo_id
                 ),
                 tbusy AS (
                     SELECT r.tenant_id, count(*) AS n FROM jobs rj
                     JOIN repos r ON r.id = rj.repo_id
                     WHERE rj.status = 'running'
                     GROUP BY r.tenant_id
                 ),
                 next AS (
                     SELECT j.id FROM jobs j
                     JOIN repos r ON r.id = j.repo_id
                     JOIN tenants t ON t.id = r.tenant_id
                     LEFT JOIN busy b ON b.repo_id = j.repo_id
                     LEFT JOIN tbusy tb ON tb.tenant_id = r.tenant_id
                     WHERE j.status = 'queued' AND j.run_after <= now()
                       AND NOT j.cancel_requested
                       AND coalesce(b.n, 0) < r.max_concurrent_jobs
                       -- A contract's cap over all its repos (#525).
                       AND (t.max_concurrent_jobs IS NULL
                            OR coalesce(tb.n, 0) < t.max_concurrent_jobs)
                       AND j.repo_id <> ALL($4)
                       -- A sub-job waits for the jobs it depends on to open
                       -- their PR (#675); it holds back no other job.
                       AND NOT EXISTS (
                           SELECT 1 FROM job_dependencies d
                           JOIN jobs p ON p.id = d.depends_on
                           WHERE d.job_id = j.id
                             AND (p.status, p.outcome) IS DISTINCT FROM ('done', 'pr_opened'))
                       AND (SELECT count(*) FROM jobs
                            WHERE status = 'running' AND locked_by = $1) < $3
                     -- By SLA (#524): P1, P2, P3, then jobs with no level;
                     -- each $6 seconds a job has waited lifts it one level,
                     -- so none waits for ever. Then the sooner deadline,
                     -- then the order they came in: FIFO without SLAs.
                     ORDER BY GREATEST(1,
                                (CASE j.priority WHEN 'P1' THEN 1 WHEN 'P2' THEN 2
                                                 WHEN 'P3' THEN 3 ELSE 4 END)
                                - floor(extract(epoch FROM now() - j.created_at)::float8 / $6::float8)::int),
                              -- At the same level, the contract running the
                              -- fewest jobs first: workers are shared (#525).
                              coalesce(tb.n, 0),
                              j.sla_deadline NULLS LAST,
                              j.id
                     LIMIT 1
                     FOR UPDATE OF j SKIP LOCKED
                 )
                 UPDATE jobs SET status = 'running', attempts = attempts + 1, locked_by = $1,
                                 locked_until = now() + make_interval(secs => $2),
                                 reason = CASE WHEN starts_with(reason, $5) THEN NULL
                                          ELSE reason END,
                                 updated_at = now()
                 FROM next WHERE jobs.id = next.id
                 RETURNING jobs.id, repo_id, issue_ref, ledger_key, source, priority, sla_deadline,
                           status, outcome, attempts, locked_by, locked_until, created_at,
                           updated_at, run_after, retries, cancel_requested, reason, pr_url,
                           retry_of, review_of, review_round
